**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] User has a 20-gallon freshwater aquarium.
- [FACT] User has a mix of neon tetras, harlequin rasboras, and a pair of fancy guppies in their aquarium.
- [FACT] User's aquarium has been set up for about 2 weeks.
- [CHANGE] User has made some adjustments to the lighting in their aquarium recently.
- [TEMPORAL] User has noticed the algae bloom for about a week.
- [PREFERENCE] User is using high-quality flake food as the main staple for their fish.
- [PREFERENCE] User supplements their fish's diet with frozen brine shrimp and bloodworms.
- [FACT] User has not tested their water parameters recently but plans to do so soon.
- [FACT] User has a standard aquarium filter and cleans it every 2 weeks.
- [FACT] User is not using any algae-preventing products currently.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested that excess nutrients from the cycling process could be causing the algae bloom.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned that insufficient biological filtration might be an issue due to the tank being only 2 weeks old.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended performing a 25-50% water change every week to reduce excess nutrients and waste products.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised monitoring water test results for ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, pH, and temperature.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested optimizing lighting by reducing duration or intensity to prevent promoting algae growth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended adding live plants to help absorb excess nutrients and reduce algae growth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided suggestions for fast-growing plants like Java moss or Anacharis.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned that upgrading to a canister filter could improve mechanical and biological filtration, helping with algae control.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant highlighted the benefits of canister filters, including improved mechanical filtration, increased biological filtration, better water circulation, and customization options.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised that adding plants to the tank can help control algae growth by competing for nutrients.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended choosing low-maintenance plants and considering the lighting conditions for plant selection.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested introducing plants gradually to the tank.
